note: Blind generalization set for the multi-reviewer pipeline. Deliberately DIFFERENT content from the 6 calibration items. Run each through POST /admin/integrated/review-debug {stem,options,answer,primary_topic,integrated_topics,integration_family,rationale} and compare live severity to expected_severity. 'kind' is the archetype. Expectations marked (INV) are safety invariants that MUST hold; (pref) are calibration preferences that may land one level off.

cases.rationale: chronic hypoxia drives pulmonary hypertension and right heart failure
cases.stem: A 70-year-old man with severe COPD and resting hypoxaemia (PaO2 52 mmHg) has cor pulmonale with peripheral oedema and a raised JVP. Left ventricular function is normal. Which intervention has been shown to improve survival in this setting?

cases.rationale: renal function constrains the safe heart-failure agent
cases.stem: A 68-year-old woman with HFrEF (EF 30%) and CKD stage 4 (eGFR 22) has serum potassium 5.4 mmol/L. She is already on maximally tolerated sacubitril/valsartan and a beta-blocker. Which addition is most appropriate to reduce mortality while respecting her renal function and potassium?

cases.rationale: diabetes vs an alternative glomerular process
cases.stem: A 55-year-old man with type 2 diabetes for 6 years presents with 3+ proteinuria. Urinalysis also shows dysmorphic red cells and red-cell casts. Blood pressure is 150/95. There is no diabetic retinopathy. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
A 60-year-old woman presents with new atrial fibrillation and a fine tremor. Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
options: Start a beta-blocker and check thyroid function

cases.stem: A 50-year-old man with CKD has serum potassium 6.8 mmol/L. His ECG is said to show prominent U waves and a prolonged QT, which in this case are the hallmark of his hyperkalaemia. Which is the most appropriate immediate treatment?

A 40-year-old woman with hyponatraemia (Na 130 mmol/L) is treated with fluid restriction. Over 24 hours her sodium rises to 132 mmol/L. She then becomes confused, and an MRI shows central pontine hyperintensity, so the team diagnoses osmotic demyelination from overcorrection. Which was the key management error?
options: No error occurred in the sodium management

cases.stem: A 58-year-old man with cirrhosis has a large-volume ascites tap. Afterwards, which measure is generally appropriate?
options: Albumin infusion to reduce post-paracentesis circulatory dysfunction
Routine broad-spectrum antibiotics for all taps

cases.rationale: immune state changes management of infection
cases.stem: A neutropenic patient (neutrophils 0.2) develops a fever of 38.5°C after chemotherapy. Which is an appropriate immediate step?
options: Wait for culture results before treating
Give paracetamol and review in the morning
